Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Every division problem can be written as a fraction and vice-versa. In this lesson, we'll extend this idea to division problems involving negative numbers.

Content:
To begin, let's find a fraction that's equivalent to the following division problem:

Content:
[MATH: (-5) \div 9]

Content:
Notice that we are dividing a negative number [MATH: {(\color{red}{-5}})] by a positive one [MATH: ({\color{blue}{9}}).] So the result will be negative:

Content:
[MATH: A]

Content:
To write down the fraction that goes in the box, recall that

Content:
[MATH: 5 \div 9 = \dfrac{5}{9}.]

Content:
Therefore, we get

Content:
[MATH: {\color{red}(-5)} \div {\color{blue}9} = {\color{red}-\dfrac{5}{9}}.]

To write down the number that goes in the box, recall that

[MATH: 1 \div 7 = \dfrac{1}{7}.]

Therefore, we get

[MATH: {\color{blue}{1}} \div {\color{red}{(-7)}} = {\color{red}-\dfrac{1}{7}}.]
